subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

You have spoilt / the little chance you / had at succeeding.
solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. No error .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence "You have spoilt the little chance you had at succeeding" is grammatically correct and free of any errors.
 
• "Spoilt" is the past participle of "spoil," and though "spoiled" is more common in American English, "spoilt" is widely accepted in British English.
 
• The phrase "the little chance you had at succeeding" correctly uses the noun phrase and relative clause without any error.
 
• The sentence meaningfully expresses that the small opportunity one had to succeed has been ruined or wasted.

Correct sentence: *You have spoilt the little chance you had at succeeding.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **British vs. American English:** "Spoilt" is used predominantly in British English, while "spoiled" is the preferred form in American English.
 
• **Past participle forms:** Both forms are grammatically correct; usage depends on the variant of English and context.
 
• **Common error checking:** Always consider the variety of English in use when evaluating words like "spoilt" vs. "spoiled."
